For more information see our Privacy StatementNews2026 Masters Tournament Coverage Overview Wednesday, March 25, 2026The 90th Masters Tournament, scheduled for April 6-12, 2026, will deliver an expansive slate of content across multiple platforms to a global audience. The full live coverage schedule is available here. A complete list of networks carrying the 2026 Masters Tournament around the world is available here. The American Forces Network will also broadcast the event to U.S. military installations throughout the world. In the United States, Amazon Prime Video will stream the Masters live on Thursday, April 9 and Friday, April 10 from 1:00 – 3:00 PM ET, leading into ESPN’s live coverage on both days from 3:00 – 7:30 PM ET. On Saturday, April 11 and Sunday, April 12, live streaming coverage will begin on Paramount+ at 12:00 PM before the Tournament airs on CBS (and continues on Paramount+) from 2:00 – 7:00 PM ET. 2026 Broadcast Schedule SiriusXM will also broadcast live Thursday, April 9 and Friday, April 10 from 2:00 – 8:00 PM ET, and on Saturday, April 11 and Sunday, April 12 from 2:00 – 7:00 PM ET. For Spanish-speaking viewers in the U.S., ESPN Deportes will air live coverage of the first and second rounds from 3:00 – 7:30 PM ET each day, the third round from 5:00 – 6:00 PM ET and the final round from 5:00 – 7:00 PM ET. Debuting this April will be Inside Amen Corner, a dedicated feed on Prime Video that will offer a stats-enhanced viewing experience and feature an in-depth look into the strategy behind Hole Nos. 11, 12 and 13. Inside Amen Corner will stream from approximately 10:45 AM – 6:00 PM ET Thursday and Friday and 11:45 AM – 6:00 PM ET Saturday and Sunday. On Wednesday, April 8, the Par 3 Contest will air from 2:00 – 4:00 PM ET on ESPN, followed by an hour-long SportsCenter at the Masters preview show at 4:00 PM ET. Coverage of the Par 3 Contest will begin at 12:00 PM ET on the ESPN App and Disney+. Welcome to the Masters will air Wednesday on ESPN from 1:00 – 2:00 PM ET and on Thursday and Friday from 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM ET as a lead-in to live coverage of the Par 3 Contest and first and second rounds. All live coverage will be available on Masters.com and the Masters App, including the broadcast, Featured Groups, Hole Nos. 4, 5 and 6, Amen Corner, Inside Amen Corner, Hole Nos. 15 and 16 and On the Range. In addition to the live-viewing experience, Masters digital platforms will offer scoring, interactive player tracking, video highlights and features, in-depth Tournament news coverage and more. Masters.com and the Masters App will continue to offer Every Shot, Every Hole at the Tournament, along with My Group, which serves as a personalized featured group for all 20,000+ videos. Range Tracker returns after making its debut in 2025 and offers access to live and recorded data on every single shot from each player during their range sessions throughout the Tournament. New for 2026, Masters Vault Search enables fans to explore and watch precise Tournament clips spanning more than 50 years of Masters final round broadcasts through simple, conversation-style prompts. Additionally, player pages now feature Every Shot, Every Hole historical video dating back to 2019. Returning this April will be Mornings at the Masters hosted by Hally Leadbetter and Roger Steele and co-produced by CBS Sports and the Masters Tournament. The daily social show will be available live Wednesday, April 8 through Sunday, April 12 from 9:00 – 9:45 AM ET via the Masters YouTube channel and will focus on the lifestyle and cultural elements of the Tournament. The Masters Tournament will deliver additional coverage through multiple content offerings, including the return of a daily, episodic series hosted by Kira K. Dixon titled Under the Umbrellas featuring guests from a variety of backgrounds. Episodes will be published to Masters YouTube beginning on Friday, April 3. Additional programming that will complement the Tournament’s coverage during Masters week will include On the Range, Practice Round Coverage, SportsCenter at the Masters, We Need to Talk at the Masters, An Invitation to the Masters: the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship, An Invitation to the Masters: the Latin America Amateur Championship, 1986 and Jim Nantz Remembers Augusta – McIlroy’s Masterpiece. The full schedule is available here. Prior to Masters week, Rory McIlroy: The Masters Wait will debut Monday, March 30 on Prime Video, while Photographer No. 24 will premiere on NBC on Sunday, April 5 at 1:00 PM ET and be available on Peacock after the initial airing. Masters fans can stay informed of news and featured content by following the Tournament on X, Instagram, Facebook, Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube and Pinterest, as well as by signing up for the Masters Newsletter. The 90th Masters is set to begin on Thursday, April 9 with Jack Nicklaus, Gary Player and Tom Watson acting as Honorary Starters. Both the Honorary Starters and Green Jacket Presentation Ceremonies will be streamed live on Masters.com, the Masters App and select Masters platforms (Facebook, X and YouTube).
